correctness.rationale: Conditioning on a record at i fixes the maximum of a uniform i-subset at i but leaves the subset uniform. The expected indicator at i differs from its unconditional mean by delta=t/n-binomial(t,i)/binomial(n,i); for earlier positions the expected number of threshold exceeders is unchanged over the entire subset, so each of the i-1 other positions has the opposite difference divided by i-1. The relative order giving R_i remains uniform even when later entries are fixed. Multiply by 1/i, with R_1 deterministic, to get the kernel. At t=0,n the threshold is constant; for 1<=t<n and i>=2 the binomial ratio is strictly less than t/n. Substituting t=j and telescoping sum_{i>j} 1/[i(i-1)] gives the column formula including j=1; at j=n the indicator is constantly zero. For interior columns j binomial(n,j)=n binomial(n-1,j-1)>=n(n-1) and j(n-1)>n, establishing their positive signs. Summation gives C_n=1/2+(1/2-B_{n-1})/n. Symmetrizing the factorial ratio for successive B_m gives the stated recurrence; it gives B_1=2, B_2=5/2, B_3=B_4=8/3 and preserves the upper bound 8/3 for m>=3. This proves all signs and the four displayed small values. Substitution gives C_{n+1}-C_n=[(n+1)B_{n-1}-2n-1]/[2n(n+1)]>0. The index pairs at 1,m-1 contribute 2/m to B_m; those at 2,m-2 contribute O(m^-2), and all deeper indices together are bounded by m/binomial(m,3). Thus C_n tends to 1/2, and the stated correlation follows from the rank-record and Eulerian marginal variances. Fresh exact enumeration of S_5 corroborated all 150 kernel entries and totals sum R=274, sum E=240, sum RE=556, giving 1/15. This is finite corroboration; the uploaded checker was read, not run.
